newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Banerj bank due to be sold off Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Banerj bank due to be sold off Wednesday.

text.p: Rio de Janeiro state government hopes to privatize its bank Banerj on Wednesday after the Senate approved a key loan clearing the way for the bank's selloff, state officials said.

The 3.09 billion reais loan to Rio state, approved by senators late Tuesday, will be used to pay off Banerj's payroll and pension-related debts, a move which was seen as key to maintain investor interest.
The auction is scheduled for 1600 local/1900 GMT on the Rio de Janeiro Stock Exchange, a spokesman for the state's Finance office said.
Late Tuesday Finance Secretary Marco Aurelio Alencar said the sale was likely to take place in the afternoon because some bureaucratic details must be settled before the auction gets underway.
Banerj's selloff, the first of a Brazilian state bank, had been originally slated for last week but the auction had to be delayed pending the Senate vote.
The state also hopes there will be no legal challenges blocking the sale. Last week, the state succeeded in lifting a court injunction suspending Banerj's privatization.
But a number of lawsuits against the auction have been filed which may delay the sale once again if any of them result in court orders at the last minute.
Four banks -- Bradesco, Banco Itau, BCN and Cia. de Investimentos Latino-American, represented by local Banco Pactual -- have signed up for the auction.
Despite the Senate approval, two of the potential buyers declined to assert they would put in a bid.
"We continue to analyse with interest the deal," said a spokesman for Banco Itau, considered the favored bidder by market analysts.
Bradesco said it was re-evaluating the deal after the Senate gave its green light to the CEF loan.
The other two bidders were not immediately available for comment.

Banerj will be offered to investors for a minimum price of 310 million reais, down from 480 million reais previously set last year when the state's first attempts to sell the bank were held up by legal challenges and debt concerns.

The state also allowed investors to pay for 100 percent of the bank's auction price with federal and state privatization bonds, which makes the bank even cheaper as those bonds can be purchased at 60-70 percent of their face value.
Banerj has been under Central Bank control since December 1994 and has been prepared for privatization by private bank Banco Bozano, Simonsen since January 1996.
The future owner of Banerj, formally known as Banco Banerj S.A., will acquire a bank with total assets of 4.5 billion reais and a net worth of 181 million reais.
